reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger, so I'll start by listing the refunds on record.

The ledger's refund list matches Alpha's handoff exactly (orders 140, 144, 145 with the same amounts), so the refund work appears consistent. Next I need the order list to know which customers to pay.

The refund list in the ledger matches Alpha's handoff exactly, so I have no concrete reason to hold. Orders show three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 38617, which is consistent with its orders minus the order 140 refund. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Acme's and birch's net balances both match their orders minus the refunds, so the figures look consistent. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance next.

I checked the net balances against the orders and refunds, and all three match: acme 45425-6808=38617, birch 55259-19464=35795, cobalt 20917-9501=11416. The refund work is consistent, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout recorded successfully. Birch's net balance of 35795 matches its orders (21876 + 33383 = 55259) minus refund 144 (19464), so I'll record that payout next.
Birch's payout recorded. Cobalt is the last customer: its orders total 20917 (8761 + 12156), minus refund 145 (9501), which gives 11416, matching net_balance. I'll record that payout.
All three payouts were recorded successfully, and each matches its net balance after the verified refunds. The batch is complete.
